This is a synthesis, not sourced data, and these are typical asking amounts for marrying-age rural families; the CAAS all-household mean is 3.9万.

discrepancies.official: NBS 70-city second-hand index, simple mean of 70 cities Dec2021->Dec2025: -20.3% (median -21.5%, range -27.9% to -1.5%)
discrepancies.assessment: At the national aggregate the official and CIA second-hand declines are similar (~-20%). The understatement claim is not supported at this level. Confidence medium: different city sets, and mean index vs average price.

discrepancies.official: NBS 70-city new-home index Dec2021->Dec2025 mean -11.3% (Shanghai +20.0%, Hangzhou +8.9%, Chengdu +7.8%, Beijing -0.7%, Shenzhen -13.6%, Guangzhou -15.7%); NBS developer average residential price 2021 10825 -> 2025 ~10005 (-7.6%)
discrepancies.assessment: New-home series are dominated by mix effects (luxury launches, price-filing limits on 备案价). The independent CIA average rises while the NBS index falls, so neither measures true like-for-like discounts. Analysts cite official new-home declines of about 20% from the 2021 peak and say real declines may be roughly double, citing off-contract discounts and price-floor guidance. That claim is commentary, low confidence.

discrepancies.official: NBS second-hand Dec2021->Dec2025: Beijing -11.2%, Shanghai -10.1%, Shenzhen -18.8%, Guangzhou -22.5%, Hangzhou -12.1%, Chengdu -1.5%, Wuhan -27.5%, Zhengzhou -25.5%
discrepancies.independent: Fortune 2023: by Aug 2023 NBS showed existing homes -6% from the Aug 2021 high, while agents and private data showed -15% to -28% in prime Shanghai, Shenzhen and Hangzhou areas; KE data showed more than half of tier-2/3 cities down more than 15%. Asia Times 2026: commentators claim many cities -40% to -50% from peak (anecdotal). 中指 Jun 2026 YoY second-hand: Nanjing -11.45%, Wuhan -10.89%, Shenzhen -5.27%.
discrepancies.assessment: Biggest plausible gap is in tier-1 and core tier-2 second-hand prices (Beijing, Shanghai, Chengdu official -1.5% to -11% over 4 years vs agent reports of -15% to -30%+). Official surveys use agency reports and field sampling, and some transaction data uses tax-filing or reference prices. Confidence medium-low on the size of the gap.

discrepancies.topic: BIS residential index (built from official data)
Household income: survey vs national accounts
discrepancies.official: NBS household survey 2023 per-capita disposable income 39218
discrepancies.independent: NBS flow-of-funds 住户部门可支配总收入 2023 = 786890.6亿 ≈ 55,800/person (my computation, population about 1.41 bn), about 1.42x the survey. Wang Xiaolu (2010) estimated 2008 hidden urban income at 9.3万亿, with top-decile income 3.2x the official figure. NBS disputed the method.
discrepancies.assessment: The survey likely understates top incomes and some property and business income; flow-of-funds includes unincorporated business surplus, so the gap is partly definitional. For game realism, the survey is fine for median households, but add a fat upper tail.

NBS non-private average 129441 (about 10.8k/month) vs private 71590 (about 6k/month) vs 农民工 5075/month. NBS excludes 个体户 and flexible workers, and the 2025 national median disposable income is 36231 per person per year. Use the private and 农民工 figures for typical workers

美团 high-frequency riders 7230-10100/month vs 南开 survey mode 6001-9000; most registered riders work under 30 days a year. Ride-hailing: research centre 7623/month (gross or net unclear) vs municipal reports of under 4000 net

CAAS rural household panel mean 3.86万 (2023) vs media/case figures of 10-30万 in hotspot provinces. The panel averages all marriages including zero or low payments; media quotes typical asking amounts in hotspots

gaps: county_price values are 二手挂牌 listing averages from a single aggregator (聚汇数据), used as a proxy for county new-home prices. No authoritative county new-home series exists. Usually only 1-2 (often poorer) prefectures were sampled per province.
